title: Global radial texture energy: are the dots packed toward the centre core or the outer rim?
question: A field of small dark dots covers a white square canvas. Looking at the whole dot field at once: are the dots packed tightly toward the centre of the canvas, forming a solid central core with the rim spread thin? Or are the dots packed toward the outside rim, forming a surrounding ring with the centre left sparse? Answer core if the dots are denser toward the centre, or rim if the dots are denser toward the outer edges.

task_signature.mechanism: Recover every dark dot from the raster, take each dot as one equal-mass mark, and measure the global radial texture-energy field: count how much of the whole constellation lies inside a central disc (relative to the shared canvas centre) versus in the surrounding annulus, and decide whether the majority mass is concentrated toward the core or toward the rim. This is a collective radial-density Gestalt of the entire field, not any single dot, its count, ink, colour, position, or overall extent.

latent_z.description: Latent scene: the set of dark dot centres and the (photometrically invisible) order in which the non-overlapping dots are painted.

boundary.observable: The answer is visible wherever the radial dot-mass comparison crosses the central-vs-outer boundary: the pixel-only arm counts dark ink inside versus outside a central disc and reads the majority, so the boundary (inner mass vs outer mass) is exposed in the raster.
boundary.quarantine: Scenes whose inner-vs-outer dot-count difference falls below 14 dots are flagged; at that near-tie the pixel arm cannot cleanly separate a core regime from a rim regime.

latent_alias.justification: The dark dots never overlap, so the order in which they are painted is photometrically invisible yet is a genuine sampled scene field. Rotating the declared dot_order list produces a byte-identical raster while analytic gold (which reads only the dot positions) is unchanged, giving a nontrivial pixel-identical tested transform.

semantic_contrast.contrast: Unlike density_gradient_direction (a monotone linear density increase along one cardinal axis) this world measures a radial, centre-vs-rim imbalance around the shared canvas centre: the decision is whether the majority of the whole field's mass is interior (core) or peripheral (rim), a radial proportion rather than a linear axis-and-sign gradient. center_surround asks whether the constellation surrounds the exact centre at all; here the constellation always spans both inner and outer regions and the question is which radial band holds the majority of the ink, independent of any polygon/concyclicity or centroid-offset selection.
semantic_contrast.expected_information_gain: Isolates whether a model can reconstruct the global radial density field of a dot cloud and compare inner-versus-outer mass into a binary core/rim regime, decoupled from linear gradient direction, surround containment, concyclicity, silhouette shape, and centroid-position selection.
